1970.notes: No tax on wages. New Hampshire taxed only interest and dividends (Interest and Dividends Tax under RSA 77, Taxation of Incomes: RSA 77:3-77:4 define taxable income as interest and dividends; the sections' source notes trace the chapter to 1923 (65:1-2) with amendments in 1931, 1933, 1955 and 1977; rate 5% from July 1, 1977 per RSA 77:1 as amended by 1977, 561:1, earlier rate not checked; not modelled). Not checked against a 1970 DRA document; the statute text and source notes are from a 2007 Wayback copy of the General Court's RSA site. RSA 77-B (Commuters Income Tax, 1970, 20:1, eff. July 1, 1970) imposed 4% on nonresidents' New Hampshire-source income (reduced to what their home state would charge) and nominally on residents' out-of-state income (satisfied by the other state's tax); it did not reach residents' New Hampshire wages and was held unconstitutional in Austin v. New Hampshire, 420 U.S. 656 (decided March 19, 1975; the opinion states New Hampshire imposed no tax on its residents' domestic earned income).
